_note: The block REGISTRY: the closed vocabulary a plan may use, in the shape of MCP-style typed tool declarations. A plan that names an unlisted block, or passes an arg outside these schemas, is REJECTED before any lowering happens — it cannot reach the renderer and fail invisibly. Note what is absent by construction: no lat/lon, no colours, no fonts, no sizes, no draw_bg.*. Those are theme or runtime concerns, so a plan is structurally incapable of getting them wrong.

PlaceRef._note: A NAME, never coordinates. The runtime geocodes. The LLM's job is disambiguation ('nvidia' -> 'Santa Clara'); turning a name into digits is not its job.

CurrentConditions._supplies: city name, hero temperature, condition row, high/low/feels line — all resolved from PlaceRef + live data

conditions._note: one per day; the only per-day thing the model knows that the data does not give as an icon

Forecast._supplies: day names from the platform calendar, lo/hi from live data, week extent from sys.weekmin/weekmax, TempBar wiring

AirQualityField._supplies: the 4x4 AQI sample grid and its 16 shader uniforms — the plan never sees a uniform

SunMoon._supplies: sunrise/sunset, daylight progress, moon phase + illumination, all computed

Details._supplies: tile captions per locale, live values, category words, colour ramp

MoversList._supplies: the 10 rows, rank/symbol/name/price/change, one cached fetch, hairlines, per-row tap targets

QuoteHeader._supplies: symbol, name, exchange, currency, price, range-aware change line + colour

PriceChart._supplies: the plot itself — StockPlot already takes semantic args, so this block is a straight pass-through. Precedent for AqiContour.

RangeChips._supplies: the chip row, selected styling from state.range, tap targets

StatGrid._supplies: tile captions per locale, live values, formatting

state._note: Weather is a pure function of (place, locale). Stocks is NOT: it has a selected ticker and a chart range that the USER changes. So a plan needs declared state, and blocks need to emit actions against it. This is the first thing the weather vocabulary could not express.

actions._note: Declared, named, and validated — a plan may only reference an action the registry defines. `select` sets state.selected, `setRange` sets state.range. The runtime owns what they DO.

views._note: Weather was one screen. Stocks is two, chosen by state. A plan lists views with a `when` predicate over state.

plans._note: Per-plan-kind requirements. The first validator hardcoded weather's: it demanded `place` and a top-level `sections`, so the stocks plan was rejected out of hand. Which was the useful failure — a generic vocabulary needs the SHAPE declared too, not just the blocks.
